purpose: Define shared identifiers, semantic domains, references, provenance and rights without using LOC1–8 as backend ownership keys. LOC1–8 are homepage/documentation guide labels only.

system_id.description: Canonical language-system identifier. Current system: lo3rwang.

domain.description: Semantic responsibility domain. Use this in backend, registries, APIs and new data instead of LOC1–8 identifiers.

related_locs.description: Legacy compatibility only. Do not add to new records.

work_id.description: Stable cross-media work identifier when the record belongs to a work.

media_id.description: Stable media-asset identifier for LOC5 or linked media.

source_refs.description: References to source files, events, works, media, URLs, or registries without duplicating their canonical content.

content_type.description: Shared routing/display type describing what the record is, independent from primary LOC ownership.

entity_id.description: Optional stable domain entity identifier when a record is not primarily a work/media/event.

governance.description: Optional shared governance envelope. Domain records may reference a separate governance-event log rather than embedding full history.

related_domains.description: Other semantic domains that analyze, reference or consume this record.

primary_loc.description: Legacy compatibility only. Do not add to new records.

governance_rules: LOC1–8 may appear on the homepage as a human-readable guide only.
Backend, registries, APIs, KM, FAQ, Search and engineering variables should use semantic domain names rather than LOC1–8 identifiers.
New records use domain and related_domains. primary_loc and related_locs are deprecated compatibility fields only.
Authority defines canonical values; consumers reference them.
Original evidence and current interpretation are separate layers; later interpretation must not silently rewrite historical source records.
Cross-domain consumers may reference or propose changes but must not overwrite another domain's authoritative record.
